ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory enhanced due diligence for Politically Exposed Persons (PEPs) under Money Laundering Prevention Act 2007. All UBOs, directors, signatories, and beneficial owners must be screened against UN Security Council Consolidated Lists, OFAC SDN List, EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, FATF Public Statements, and Samoa Ministry of Finance domestic sanctions register. Real-time electronic name and date-of-birth matching is required; adverse hits escalate to the Financial Intelligence Unit (FIU) of Samoa within statutory thresholds. The AML/CFT compliance programme must include ongoing transaction monitoring and risk-based enhanced measures for any sanction-relevant jurisdiction.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Samoa Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour (MCIL) – Integrity Portal / International Companies Registry (ICR) online name clearance system
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Company names must be in English or provide a verified English transliteration for names in Chinese or other scripts. International Companies may have a Samoan-language name where there is a precise English version. The standard corporate identifier 'Limited', 'Ltd', 'Corporation', 'Inc', 'Pty Ltd', or 'International Company' is mandatory. The Registrar will reject any name that is not visually clear, can be transliterated into the Latin alphabet, or breaches public order / national symbols.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If a name is rejected, the applicant must wait for a statutory notice from the Companies Registry specifying the refusal basis, and may within 14 calendar days thereafter file a formal written appeal to the Registrar of International Companies via a licensed registered agent. The appeal must propose a curative modification or legal justification. The Registrar must decide within 21 working days. A fresh name reservation application is available after the rejection decision is exhausted or withdrawn. If the Registrar remains unsatisfied, the applicant may petition the Supreme Court of Samoa for judicial review within 30 days.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permissible and ordinary. An International Company must maintain a physical registered office at the address of its licensed registered agent in Samoa. Day-to-day management may be performed entirely virtually and the CFO services may be outsourced from abroad. The registered office perfoms statutory records-holding and service-of-process functions only. For the described virtual CFO/business services, no physical in-country presence is mandatory.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Quantified risk: 8%–12% annually. Registrar issues pro-active compliance audits for international companies engaged in financial/accounting outsourcing; however, low-risk virtual CFO or bookkeeping services without custodial client funds carry a lower unannounced-inspection rate. The registered agent may conduct an independent eligibility visit or remote verification in accordance with AML/CFT obligations.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: International Companies Act 1987 (Samoa), as amended by the International Companies (Amendment) Act 2015; ss. 7-9 (incorporation), s. 12 (business activities), s. 127A (licensing); supplemented by the Companies Act 2001 (mutatis mutandis) and the Money Laundering Prevention Act 2007
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registrar of International Companies, Samoa International Financial Services Authority (SIFSA), Apia, Samoa
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Registration as an International Company (Form IC-1)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital; a single subscriber share of no par value may be allotted for USD 1.00. No escrow or paid-in capital deposit is required for an International Company.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED THAT the subscriber, having executed the Memorandum and Articles of Association, is hereby allotted one fully paid ordinary share in the capital of the Company for the sum of USD 1.00. RESOLVED FURTHER THAT the registered office of the Company is fixed at the offices of the Licensed Registered Agent in Apia, Samoa, and the Registered Agent is authorized to file the Application for Incorporation with the SIFSA Registrar. RESOLVED FURTHER THAT the initial Directors and Officers are appointed with power to open bank accounts, execute client contracts, and deliver fractional CFO advisory and bookkeeping services, and the Corporate Secretary shall issue authorized signatory lists to financial institutions.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name Clearance and Corporate Name Reservation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Samoa International Financial Services Authority (SIFSA) - Corporate Names Unit, Apia, Samoa
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The Licensed Registered Agent submits a name reservation request through the SIFSA online registry portal or lodges Form IC-R with the Corporate Names Unit. Verify that the proposed corporate name is not identical or confusingly similar to an existing local or international company name and does not contain prohibited terms such as 'bank', 'insurance', or 'trust' unless separately licensed. Provide at least two alternative names in descending order of preference.
required_dossiers: Name reservation request (Form IC-R)
Certified passport copy of the beneficial owner
Registered Agent engagement letter
Due diligence and source-of-funds summary
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused, file an amended name reservation within one business day; no additional Government fee is levied for the first alternative name. An administrative refusal may be appealed to the Registrar in writing within 14 days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting of Memorandum and Articles of Association and Governance Instruments
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Licensed Registered Agent (corporate secretarial department) under SIFSA supervision, Apia, Samoa
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The Registered Agent prepares the Memorandum and Articles of Association in English adopting the Model Articles for International Companies, including the registered office clause, share structure of one no-par value share, indemnity provisions, and an elective clause confirming that no domestic Samoan business activity will be conducted. The sole director executes the consent forms and the subscriber signs the subscription page. The documents are notarized and counter-sealed by the Registered Agent.
required_dossiers: Memorandum and Articles of Association in English
Form IC-A (Consent of Registered Agent)
Form IC-B (Consent of First Director(s) and Secretary)
Subscriber resolution adopting the Memorandum and Articles
Proof of physical registered office address in Apia
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If SIFSA queries any clause of the Memorandum and Articles, the Registered Agent files a supplementary deed to amend or substitute the offending clause; no fresh Government fee is charged for minor amendments made within 30 days of initial filing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing of Incorporation Application with the Registrar
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registrar of International Companies, Samoa International Financial Services Authority (SIFSA) - Apia Head Office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the completed Application for Registration as an International Company (Form IC-1) together with the signed Memorandum and Articles and supporting consents to the SIFSA Registrar. The filing may be completed electronically via the SIFSA digital portal with notarized PDF attachments. The State filing fee of USD 200 is paid by bank transfer or SWIFT to the SIFSA designated Treasury account; the first annual licence fee is paid concurrently.
required_dossiers: Form IC-1 (Application for Registration)
Signed Memorandum and Articles of Association
Form IC-A and Form IC-B consents
Certificate of Good Standing of the Registered Agent
Receipt of USD 200 Government filing fee
Registered office physical address attestation
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar issues a requisition, correct the deficient items within 21 days by submitting a cure letter and revised form; if the 21-day deadline is missed, a new application must be filed with a fresh fee.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Issuance of Certificate of Incorporation and Tax Exemption Certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registrar of International Companies, SIFSA; Samoa Ministry of Revenue
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon satisfactory review, the Registrar issues the Certificate of Incorporation under the seal of SIFSA, evidencing the company's separate legal personality. The company simultaneously receives a Tax Exemption Certificate confirming exemption from Samoan income tax on foreign-source income and stamp duty under the International Companies Act 1987. The Certificate includes the Company Registration Number and the registered office at the Registered Agent's address.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation (original)
Tax Exemption Certificate
Registry extract showing directors and shareholders
Company seal certification (if requested)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Certificate contains a typographical or legal-name error, return the original within 10 business days for reissuance at no cost; substantive corrections require a Special Resolution and a Registry filing fee of USD 50.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Governance Activation, Officer Designation, and AML/CFT Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: SIFSA Compliance and Enforcement Division; Samoa Financial Intelligence Unit
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Hold the first board meeting or adopt a written unanimous resolution to approve the share allotment, adopt the registered office, appoint the CFO Service Director, Money Laundering Reporting Officer, and Corporate Secretary, and open bank accounts with a licensed international bank. File Form IC-7 (Appointment of Officers) and register the beneficial ownership statement with the Financial Intelligence Unit under the Money Laundering Prevention Act 2007. A wholly external non-resident clientele ordinarily triggers only an AML-exempt classification.
required_dossiers: Minutes or Written Resolution of First Board Meeting
Form IC-7 (Officer Appointment Notification)
Consent and due diligence file of each officer
Beneficial ownership register extract
AML/CFT risk assessment narrative (Low Risk Standard)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Where the Financial Intelligence Unit requests further beneficial ownership detail, supplement the register file within 14 days; late filing of Form IC-7 attracts a penalty of USD 100, which may be remitted by showing reasonable cause.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Industrial and Physical Licensing Clearances for Office-Based Activity
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: SIFSA Licensing Division; Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour; Samoa Fire and Emergency Services Authority
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Because virtual CFO services are dematerialized, apply for an International Company Business Licence (Class B - Professional Services) with SIFSA and the Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour, specifying 'Fractional CFO Advisory, Management Accounting and Multicurrency Bookkeeping'. For the Apia registered office, obtain a Certificate of Premises Registration from the Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour, an electrical certificate of compliance, and a Samoa Fire and Emergency Services Authority fire safety certificate. Secure professional indemnity insurance; if staff are employed in Samoa, register with the Samoa National Provident Fund and the Accident Compensation Corporation.
required_dossiers: Business Licence application form
Certificate of Incorporation copy
Fire Safety Certificate for registered office
Electrical Certificate of Compliance
Professional Indemnity insurance certificate (minimum USD 500,000)
Registered office lease or premises permission
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the licence is declined owing to a territorial activity restriction, restructure the licence application to 'offshore clientele only' and annex the Tax Exemption Certificate; a written appeal may be lodged with the Minister of Commerce within 21 days.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Samoa International Financial Services Authority (SIFSA) Licensing Division, in coordination with the Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour (MCIL) General Business Licence Unit
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: International Company Business Licence - Class B (Professional Services: Fractional CFO Advisory and Multicurrency Bookkeeping)

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministry of Natural Resources and Environment (MNRE), Samoa - Planning and Urban Management Agency
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt: administrative office use under the Planning and Urban Management Act 2004; no EIA or development consent required for the virtual service model
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not applicable - zero wastewater, VOC or solid industrial waste streams. Digital record retention standards under the International Companies Act 1987 Record-Keeping Rules and client financial data protection standards apply.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire Safety Certificate from the Samoa Fire and Emergency Services Authority for the registered office; electrical certificate of compliance; occupational safety and health workplace registration with the Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour; professional indemnity insurance coverage of minimum USD 500,000.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Samoa Revenue Authority (SRA), Apia, Samoa; online portal: https://www.sra.gov.ws
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A Samoa International Company (IC) is exempt from income tax and VAGST on offshore business and is not ordinarily required to hold a local TIN. Where a TIN is nonetheless needed (e.g., customs clearance, opening a domestic bank account, or engaging in local transactions), the foreign entity must file SRA Form TIN-01 (Taxpayer Identification Number Registration) with the Samoa Revenue Authority, accompanied by: (i) certified copy of the International Company certificate of incorporation; (ii) memorandum and articles of association; (iii) current certificate of good standing from the Samoa International Financial Services Authority (SIFSA); (iv) certified passport copies of directors/shareholders; (v) proof of the licensed registered agent in Samoa; and (vi) a copy of the registered office address. Applications are submitted in person or through the licensed registered agent. A TIN is issued within 5–10 business days upon complete filing and verification. Approval is at the discretion of the Commissioner of the SRA; non-resident entities are treated as non-residents for domestic tax purposes.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No check-the-box or hybrid mismatch election exists for a Samoa International Company. Tax status is statutory: an IC that complies with the International Companies Act 2017 and receives only offshore income is automatically exempt from income tax, stamp duty, and VAGST on its offshore business (exemption available without election). An IC that elects to carry on business in Samoa with Samoan persons or devolves into domestic trading loses the exemption and becomes subject to ordinary Samoan income tax and the Value Added Goods and Services Tax (VAGST) Act 2008. No CFC-payment or conduit election is available to ICs.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAGST (Value Added Goods and Services Tax)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: SAT 100,000 of annual taxable turnover (a person making or intending to make taxable supplies exceeding SAT 100,000 in any 12-month period must compulsorily register; voluntary registration is available)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No real-time fiscal clearance or digital stamping mandate is in force in Samoa. The SRA does not require API-based continuous clearance of e-invoices. Taxpayers may issue ordinary commercial invoices manually or electronically. Mandatory content for VAGST invoices: the seller's name and TIN, buyer's name, invoice date, description of goods/services, quantity and price, amount of VAGST charged, and total amount (for exempt supplies, a statement that VAGST is not charged). All VAT returns and payments must be filed electronically through the SRA's tax administration portal, but invoice clearance is not automated.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: A Samoa International Company may zero-rate its VAGST supplies if it is registered (or voluntarily registered) and the services qualify as exported services: (i) the services are supplied to a non-resident who is outside Samoa at the time of supply; (ii) the services are not supplied for use or consumption in Samoa; and (iii) the services are directly connected with movable property or intangible property situated or used outside Samoa, or relate to a business carried on entirely outside Samoa. Fractional CFO advisory, remote bookkeeping, and multicurrency ledger services delivered by a Samoa IC to overseas clients fall within the zero-rating category if no part of the service is consumed in Samoa and the recipient is a non-resident outside Samoa. The IC must hold the standard export substantiation pack as set out below.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (SRA/Customs Form Cus-Decl) for goods; not applicable to pure services — for services, an SRA-issued Export Services Declaration or service export notification is required
Commercial invoice and detailed service contract (describing the offshore nature of the service)
Evidence of recipient non-residence: certificate of incorporation of the foreign client or utility bill/lease outside Samoa
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill (for physical exports only)
Inward Remittance Certificate or bank SWIFT credit advice evidencing full payment of the invoice in foreign currency from outside Samoa
Proof of delivery/use outside Samoa: signed service completion report or counterparty acknowledgment
Foreign currency purchase/sale confirmation from a licensed Samoan bank where applicable
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The Samoa Revenue Authority may audit any zero-rated export claim within the 4-year assessment window and review exchange control documentation to verify that export proceeds were received within 180 days. A failed or fraudulent zero-rating claim triggers full clawback of the uncharged VAGST at 15% plus late payment penalty of 1.5% per month (or part thereof) and default interest at the statutory rate; where fraud or gross negligence is established, a civil penalty of up to 300% of the tax evaded can be imposed, in addition to criminal liability of up to SAT 50,000 fine and 7 years' imprisonment per the Tax Administration Act 2016 and VAGST Act 2008. For International Companies, loss of the IC tax exemption is also possible if the activity is deemed to be domestic trading in Samoa.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Central Bank of Samoa (CBS; Faletupe Tutotonu o Samoa) — statutory exchange-control authority under the Exchange Control Act 1976, with delegated authorized-dealer powers exercised by licensed commercial banks.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Samoan Tala (ISO 4217: WST) is a partially convertible Pacific currency: current-account remittances are approved by authorized dealers against documented trade or services invoices, while capital-account transfers and current payments above CBS-published thresholds require prior Central Bank of Samoa (CBS) approval. Profit remittance for an onshore licensed enterprise requires a Ministry-of-Revenue tax-clearance certificate and CBS filing; the International Company, by contrast, is tax-exempt and, under the International Companies Act 1987, lies outside CBS exchange control for all offshore business so long as it does not deal with Samoan residents. The residual convertibility hurdle is market depth: WST has no offshore interbank liquidity, conversion spreads widen materially above WST 1 million equivalent, and Samoan banks apply Enhanced Due Diligence to offshore IC treasury flows.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: The Exchange Control Regulations 1980 require goods-export proceeds to be fully repatriated within 180 days from shipment and surrendered to an authorized dealer within 28 days of receipt; the mandatory conversion ratio is a CBS policy parameter (current practice permits retention in a foreign-currency deposit account, with a continuing notification duty). Services receipts (ISIC 6920 fractional CFO fees) are invisible earnings: an onshore entity must route them through an authorized dealer against invoice evidence, but they are outside the 28-day goods-surrender regime. The Samoan International Company is wholly excluded where it has no resident trade: virtual-CFO fees may be collected offshore with no surrender or conversion requirement, and funds brought into Samoa may be held in foreign-currency deposit accounts free of mandatory conversion.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Return and payment of International Company annual government fee (Form IC-AR)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Samoa International Finance Authority (SIFA) – Registrar of International Companies
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 days after each anniversary of incorporation; no fixed calendar date
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: 10% late-payment penalty per month (US$100 minimum); arrears unpaid for 6 consecutive months subject the IC to administrative strike-off by the Registrar; restoration requires payment of all arrears plus US$300 reinstatement fee

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Registered Agent Annual Compliance Confirmation (KYC/UBO and registered office verification)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Licensed Samoa registered agent (agent-to-registrar confirmation), to be produced to SIFA on demand
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before each incorporation anniversary; agent must re-verify beneficial owners within 14 days of any share transfer
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Agent non-compliance may incur SIFA administrative penalties or cancellation of agent licence; company remains subject to strike-off if confirmation is withheld for more than 6 months

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Economic Substance/Residency Notification (if a relevant activity such as a headquarters or service centre is carried on)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Samoa International Finance Authority – Economic Substance Unit
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 12 months after the end of the accounting period (aligning with the IC's declared financial year)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to notify triggers SIFA penalty of US$500 plus up to US$10,000 for inaccurate material particulars; persistent default may result in exchange of information with foreign tax authorities and administrative dissolution

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No compulsory audit for a private International Company; audit is mandatory only for licensed banks, insurers or public companies, or when shareholders holding at least 10% of voting shares request an independent audit within 14 days after circulation of the financial statements
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS (International Financial Reporting Standards); books and records may be maintained in any currency but must be capable of producing IFRS-compliant statements; US GAAP may be adopted equivalently for offshore ICs

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: At each anniversary the registered agent circulates an annual confirmation for signature by the director and each beneficial owner certifying that the Registers are accurate; any share transfer or change of members/directors must be recorded in the statutory registers and notified to the Registrar within 14 days of the register entry, with the agent retaining current KYC/UBO documentation under Samoa AML/CFT rules

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 800–1,500 per annum for licensed registered agent and registered-office services
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 3,000–8,000 if a shareholder-requested audit is triggered; not required for a standard exempt IC

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 25% (Income Tax Act 2015 (Samoa), s.73(1)). A company incorporated in Samoa is tax resident and nominally taxable on worldwide income, but this entity is an International Company (IC) under the International Companies Act 1987 (as amended) and, while holding a valid Tax Exemption Certificate, is taxable at 0% on qualified income derived from outside Samoa.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: International Company statutory exemption under s.203 of the International Companies Act 1987: exemption from income tax, stamp duty and related Samoan taxes for up to 20 years for a qualifying IC, conditional on maintaining a registered office and licensed registered agent in Samoa and deriving no Samoa-source income. Zero tax applies to offshore Virtual CFO subscription fees, fractional CFO advisory fees, multicurrency bookkeeping and ledger fees, interest, dividends, royalties and capital gains sourced outside Samoa. No GST/VAT on exported services, no capital gains tax, no estate or wealth tax. Residual 25% exposure is limited to income sourced in Samoa (e.g., services rendered to Samoa-resident clients) and to profits re-sourced by the General Anti-Avoidance Rule.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form CIT-IC (Annual Corporation Tax Return - International Company), filed through the Samoa Revenue Authority (SRA) Online Taxpayer Services portal administered by the Ministry of Revenue, Apia.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The tax year is the calendar year (1 January to 31 December); the return must be lodged on or before 30 June of the year following the tax year (i.e., within 6 months after year-end) and any resulting tax paid by the same date. A tax-exempt IC with no Samoa-source income is not required to make a provisional payment but should file the exemption declaration section annually upon SRA request.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal entity name, Taxpayer Identification Number (TIN), International Company Registration Number, and Samoan registered office address.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter the IC registration number and SRA TIN; provide the licensed Samoan registered agent's name and address as the authorised contact point for all revenue correspondence.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax Exemption Certificate reference and exemption commencement date under the International Companies Act 1987.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Attach a copy of the Tax Exemption Certificate; if the certificate has lapsed or been revoked, this return must be prepared on the fully taxable basis at 25%.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total gross income derived worldwide during the tax year, split into Samoa-source and foreign-source income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Foreign-source Virtual CFO and bookkeeping fees must be separately scheduled as exempt; Samoa-source fees (services performed while the director, CFO or personnel are physically in Samoa or performed for Samoa-resident clients) must be declared in the taxable column.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Related-party cross-border transaction value (in WST) for transfer pricing schedule.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Disclose all intercompany management fees, software subscriptions, payment-rail charges (Stripe Billing, Wise) and subcontracting payments to related entities; attach the TP schedule where the WST 500,000 threshold is exceeded.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Withholding tax withheld on payments to non-residents (dividends, interest, royalties).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Declare and remit 15% WHT on any taxable distribution to a non-resident shareholder, or 0% where the distribution is sourced from the exempt offshore fund; treaty-reduced rates are admissible only with a valid Tax Residency Certificate.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income after exemptions and tax payable at 25%.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a fully compliant exempt IC the amount is nil; for an IC whose exemption has been partially denied, tax is computed only on the Samoan-sourced profit after applying the 5-year loss carryforward.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing attracts a penalty of 5% of the tax payable for each month or part of a month, capped at 50%, plus a flat late-filing penalty of WST 1,000 for exempt ICs failing to file the nil/exempt declaration. Late payment accrues a 2% monthly (12% per annum) surcharge. Understatement of the exemption characterisation triggers a 100% shortfall penalty on the avoided tax, fines up to WST 1,000,000, and criminal prosecution where intent is established.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form CIT-EST (Quarterly Estimated Tax Declaration), also filed through the SRA Online Taxpayer Services portal.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Quarterly installments are due on 30 September, 31 December, 31 March and 30 June of the tax year. An IC deriving no Samoa-source income and holding a valid exemption certificate is not obliged to pay installments but should lodge a nil declaration to maintain its taxpayer compliance record.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Estimated taxable Samoa-source income for the current tax year.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Insert nil for an exempt offshore IC; otherwise compute the estimate on arm's length adjusted profit before the 25% rate.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Quarterly installment tax payable (25% applied to estimated annual taxable income, apportioned quarterly).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a non-resident-owned IC, ensure that the payment is funded from the Samoan bank account of the entity and that the bank remittance reference states the tax type and TIN.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Declaration of exemption status and Tax Exemption Certificate reference.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Confirm that no change of control, new Samoan-resident client, or relocation of management into Samoa has occurred during the quarter; any such change invalidates the exemption declaration retroactively.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Non-payment or late payment of quarterly installments attracts a 2% monthly penalty on the unpaid amount and statutory interest; persistent non-compliance triggers Director Penalty Notices, a negative tax clearance certificate, and suspension of the entity's payment-rail and banking activity due to SRA enforcement action.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 15% withholding tax on dividends paid by a resident company (Income Tax Act 2015). A qualifying exempt International Company distributing profits accumulated entirely from offshore sources pays 0% Samoan dividend WHT because the distribution is sourced from the exempt offshore fund. Where the IC's profits have been re-characterised as Samoan-source, the 15% rate applies to dividend payments to non-resident shareholders; under an applicable comprehensive DTA (e.g., the Samoa-China DTA), the rate may be reduced to 5% where the beneficial owner is a company holding directly at least 25% of the voting capital, otherwise 10%.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Step 1: confirm that the relevant DTA is in force and that the recipient is the beneficial owner. Step 2: obtain a Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) from the home revenue authority and a completed beneficial-owner declaration. Step 3: submit the certified TRC, shareholding structure diagram, and SRA Form WHT-DTA to the paying Samoan company (or to SRA for an advance ruling) before or at the time of payment. Step 4: the payer may apply the reduced treaty rate only upon receipt of the TRC and the declaration; SRA will reverse treaty relief retroactively if the TRC is not genuine or the declaration is false. A foreign recipient that suffered the full 15% may file a refund application with SRA within 3 years of the end of the tax year in which the WHT was paid.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory rates under the Income Tax Act 2015: 15% for royalty income and 15% for interest income paid to non-residents. Under the Samoa-China DTA, interest may be taxed at 10% and royalties at 10% where the recipient is the beneficial owner. The royalty definition covers payments for the use of, or right to use, intellectual property, software, and technical know-how; Virtual CFO fees that are purely professional bookkeeping or management consultancy fees are treated as business profits rather than royalties, but SRA will pierce arrangements in which consulting fees are split or inflated to conceal royalty or diverted-profit transfers. Interest paid by a resident bank to a non-resident may be exempt in specific negotiated financings, but the general non-resident WHT default is 15%.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: WST 500,000: aggregate cross-border related-party transaction value per annum above which the International Company must maintain contemporaneous Transfer Pricing Documentation (Local File) covering its Virtual CFO and bookkeeping service lines, including functional analysis, benchmarking study, and arm's length pricing justification. A group-wide Master File should be prepared where the MNE group's consolidated revenue exceeds WST 5,000,000 or where the ultimate parent is resident in a jurisdiction applying the OECD EUR 750 million filing threshold. Documentation must be delivered to SRA within 30 days of a written request.
approved_arm_length_methodologies: Comparable Uncontrolled Price (CUP) - preferred where the Virtual CFO subscription fee is verifiable against standalone third-party pricing
Resale Price Method (RPM) - applied when the Samoan IC resells services purchased from a related provider
Cost Plus Method (CPM) - used for cost-reimbursed fractional CFO support agreements
Transactional Net Margin Method (TNMM) - the default method for multicurrency bookkeeping and back-office KPO functions using benchmarked net margins
Profit Split Method (PSM) - appropriate where the Samoan IC and related parties jointly contribute intangibles and risk in an integrated Virtual CFO engagement
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Samoa has not enacted a BVI-style Economic Substance Regulations statute, but the IC tax exemption is substance-conditioned. The International Companies Act 1987 (as amended in 2015) requires a registered office, a licensed Samoa registered agent, a directors' register, and accessible corporate records in Samoa. The Income Tax Act 2015 General Anti-Avoidance Rule (ss.92-93) empowers SRA to disregard an IC lacking economic substance and to tax its profits at 25% where control, management, staff and value creation occur in Samoa. Samoa's OECD Global Forum and BEPS Inclusive Framework commitments require genuine economic activity and exchange of information on request. A credible Virtual CFO substance profile must include board-approved service contracts, professional fee records, segregated multicurrency ledgers, documentary evidence of the client engagement and delivery jurisdiction, and arm's length charging for any intercompany software, payment-rail, or subcontracting services.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Classifying substantial fee income from Virtual CFO and bookkeeping services actually performed for Samoa-resident clients, or controlled and managed from Samoa, as tax-exempt foreign-source income on the IC annual return; backdating client service contracts; invoicing through the IC without operational substance; knowingly concealing Samoan-source revenue from the Samoa Revenue Authority.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Shortfall penalty of 100% of the avoided tax plus monthly deferral interest of 2% under the Tax Administration Act 2015; administrative fine up to WST 1,000,000; criminal prosecution with fines up to WST 1,000,000 and imprisonment up to 7 years; immediate cancellation of the IC Tax Exemption Certificate; recovery of all previously claimed exempt taxes; compulsory deregistration.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors, virtual CFOs and tax agents who caused or acquiesced in the false characterisation are jointly and severally liable for the company's unpaid tax through piercing of the corporate veil; courts may order civil restitution of diverted profits; travel bans and departure prohibitions may be imposed; director disqualification for up to 5 years; imprisonment is additional and not dischargeable by corporate liquidation.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating as a letterbox IC: no active Samoan registered office, no licensed registered agent, no board minutes, no business premises or professional records, no transfer pricing analysis, and no real capability to perform the Virtual CFO function attributed to Samoa while profits are stripped offshore to zero-tax beneficiaries.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Strike-off and deregistration under the International Companies Act 1987; revocation of the Tax Exemption Certificate; SRA re-assessment of all profits at 25% plus the 100% evasion penalty; registration of enforcement charges against assets held by nominees; fines up to WST 100,000 per contravention; prohibition from opening or maintaining bank accounts in Samoa.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be publicly named and disqualified for up to 5 years; liquidators may set aside sham arrangements as void against the company; directors are liable for company debts where the IC traded while insolvent and failed to remit tax; de facto responsible persons are personally assessed for unpaid tax; travel bans and contempt proceedings apply where corporate books are not produced.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to maintain an accurate beneficial ownership register or to appoint a licensed Samoa registered agent; accepting funds through Stripe Billing or Wise without customer due diligence and source-of-funds verification; routing client money through unlicensed payment intermediaries; acting as Virtual CFO for shell entities to launder criminal proceeds; undeclared nominee shareholding arrangements.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Act 2007 (as amended): fines up to WST 1,000,000 for the company and WST 500,000 for each officer per breach; freezing and confiscation of the IC's bank and payment-rail accounts; suspension or revocation of any required financial service registration; additional SRA penalties for failure to obtain or renew a TIN.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and compliance officers face imprisonment up to 14 years for money laundering or facilitation, personal fines, travel bans, seizure of personal assets, and permanent disqualification from managing regulated entities in Samoa and DTA/counterparty jurisdictions.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Withholding Tax Defaults on Profit Repatriation
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Paying dividends, royalties or interest to non-resident shareholders and related parties without withholding the statutory 15% WHT; claiming treaty-reduced rates without an SRA-recognised Tax Residency Certificate or beneficial-owner declaration; mischaracterising distributions as management fees, consultancy retainers, loan repayments or software licensing fees to avoid WHT.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: WHT shortfall penalty of 20% of the unremitted amount plus interest at 2% per month; the grossed-up distribution is denied as a deduction and may be re-characterised as a deemed dividend taxable in the hands of the Samoan entity; criminal fines up to WST 1,000,000; imprisonment up to 7 years for fraudulent evasion of withholding obligations.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly failed to withhold or remit are personally liable as persons deemed to have collected the tax; civil restitution proceedings may be brought by affected shareholders; travel restriction orders are routinely issued; personal liability is not discharged by liquidation or by resignation after the default date.
